value.note: Same 3225 four-pad outline as the 12 MHz sibling: two crystal terminals plus two shield pads that must be grounded. The footprint is interchangeable between the two parts even though their electrical parameters are not.

source.ref: Package SMD3225-4P; JLCPCB catalog record joints = 4

value.note: 16 MHz is the classic ATmega328P speed, and per the AVR speed grades it requires at least 4.5 V — at 3.3 V the device is limited to 10 MHz, so this crystal only belongs on a 5 V AVR board. Second most stocked crystal in the JLCPCB catalog at 443,913 units and a Basic part.

source.ref: Specifications: Frequency = 16MHz; catalog record stock 443913, basic = 1

value.note: CL = 9 pF — less than half the 20 pF of the 12 MHz part in the same package and series. A 22 pF load-capacitor pair, the reflex choice for AVR boards, would be badly wrong here: with CL = 9 pF and 5 pF of stray capacitance the external capacitors work out around 8 pF each, not 22 pF. This is the single strongest argument for recording CL per part rather than treating crystals as interchangeable.

50 ohm, exactly at the RP2040's stated 50 ohm ceiling — though 16 MHz is not an RP2040 frequency, so that comparison is informational. Notably better than the 12 MHz sibling's 80 ohm despite the identical package and series, which is a reminder that ESR tracks the individual part rather than the outline. Value taken from the LCSC product-page specification table because the catalog dump omits ESR and the LCSC datasheet link returns an HTML interstitial.

value.note: Room-temperature tolerance; add the +/-20 ppm stability for the worst case.
Drift over -40 to +85 degC, giving about +/-30 ppm worst case in total. Adequate for an AVR running UART at standard baud rates, where the tolerance budget is percent-level rather than ppm-level.
